title: Homotopy uniqueness of Cartan--Eilenberg comparison lifts
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be abelian categories with enough injectives, let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an exact additive functor, and let $K^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$ be cochain complexes in $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ with $K^p=L^p=0$ for $p<0$. Let $I_K$ be a Cartan--Eilenberg injective resolution of $K^\bullet$ and $J_L$ one of $L^\bullet$ [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists], with augmentations $\epsilon_K:K^\bullet\to I_K^{\bullet,0}$ and $\epsilon_L:L^\bullet\to J_L^{\bullet,0}$. Let $u,u':F(K^\bullet)\to L^\bullet$ be homotopic complex maps, with homotopy $s:F(K^p)\to L^{p-1}$, and let $\phi,\psi:F(I_K)\to J_L$ be morphisms of double complexes whose augmentations satisfy $\phi\,F(\epsilon_K)=\epsilon_L\,u$ and $\psi\,F(\epsilon_K)=\epsilon_L\,u'$. Then there is a homotopy $H$ between the induced total-complex maps, so $\operatorname{Tot}(\phi)-\operatorname{Tot}(\psi)=dH+Hd$, and $H(F^q\operatorname{Tot}^n)\subseteq F^{q-1}\operatorname{Tot}^{n-1}$ for the decreasing filtration $F$ by resolution degree [def-sp-filtration]. In particular, when $u=u'$ one may take $s=0$ and the two comparison maps are homotopic by a homotopy lowering resolution degree by one.

source.place: Lemma 015I (lemma-cartan-eilenberg), comparison morphism construction, and Remark 015K (remark-functorial-ss)

proof.text: Put $\delta=\phi-\psi$. Additivity makes $\delta$ a morphism of double complexes, and the augmentation identities give $\delta F(\epsilon_K)=\epsilon_L(u-u')=\epsilon_L(ds+sd)$. Thus the induced map on the augmented degree-zero complexes has the prescribed null-homotopy $s$.

source.place: Lemma 015I and Remark 015K, comparison morphism construction

proof.text: Check the repaired double-complex lemma hypotheses for $F(I_K)$ and $J_L$. Exactness of the augmented boundary, cycle, and horizontal-cohomology rows of $F(I_K)$, and of $0\to Z\to F(I_K)\to B\to0$, follows from exactness of $F$ and the Cartan--Eilenberg resolution $I_K$; the corresponding rows of $J_L$ are injective resolutions by [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists]. With $w=u-u'$ and the given homotopy $s$, the augmentation identity is $\delta F(\epsilon_K)=\epsilon_L w$, where $\delta=\phi-\psi$. Thus [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-double-complex-homotopy] applies and supplies both homotopy components.

source.place: Lemma 015I comparison construction by B, Z, H rows and Remark 015K; horizontal/vertical homotopy decomposition as in Weibel Lemma 5.7.10

proof.text: The repaired lemma gives maps $s_1^{p,q}:F(I_K^{p,q})\to J_L^{p-1,q}$ and $s_2^{p,q}:F(I_K^{p,q})\to J_L^{p,q-1}$, with $s_1$ restricting on the augmented row to the prescribed $s$ and with the component identities required for the total homotopy.

source.place: Lemma 015I, compatibility with the second exact sequence and vertical differential; Remark 015K

proof.text: Set $H^{p,q}=s_1^{p,q}+(-1)^p s_2^{p,q}$. The component equations in the preceding step give $d_{\operatorname{Tot}J}H+Hd_{\operatorname{Tot}F(I_K)}=\delta$; hence $\operatorname{Tot}(\phi)-\operatorname{Tot}(\psi)=dH+Hd$. The horizontal part preserves the vertical degree and the vertical part lowers it by one, so for the decreasing filtration by vertical (resolution) degree, $H(F^q\operatorname{Tot}^n)\subseteq F^{q-1}\operatorname{Tot}^{n-1}$ [def-sp-double-complex-total, def-sp-filtration]. If $u=u'$, choose $s=0$ and obtain the final assertion.
